subject.title: Make the Crabbox skill portable and automate pinned downstream snapshots

question: Should this repository own a standardized opt-in downstream snapshot contract for Crabbox, or should consumer repositories keep explicit repository-local adaptations without a shared updater?
rationale: The request creates a durable cross-repository API and automation contract, including the acceptable boundary between canonical shared policy and downstream-specific commands; source-level implementation alone cannot determine that ownership policy.

options.title: Sponsor a pinned snapshot contract
options.body: Define a portable shared skill, pin-manifest format, verifier, and PR-only updater pattern with consumer opt-in and documented overrides.

options.title: Keep consumer adaptations independent
options.body: Retain the current canonical skill but require each downstream repository to own and review any local Crabbox guidance separately.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a pinned snapshot contract
recommendation.body: Define a portable shared skill, pin-manifest format, verifier, and PR-only updater pattern with consumer opt-in and documented overrides.

likelyOwner.reason: As the repository-member proposer who documented the downstream compatibility constraints and prior correction history, they are the clearest available routing candidate for the initial direction decision.
